mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell sharply to -15.3 at t-1w then rebounded to -10.4 at t-0w, consistent with a transient shock that is already reverting toward its pre-shock trend; this mean-reversion pattern should continue, pulling the next 28-day average above the last 28-day average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC recovered from -15.3 to -10.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise above the -10.4 to -15.3 range and instead trends further negative over the next 4 weeks, showing no reversion.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT decline exceeding 20 points signals active tightening of mobility restrictions or public caution, which suppresses discretionary retail and recreation trips over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -31.4 at t-3w to -44.6 at t-1w, a decline exceeding 20 points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT having fallen more than 20 points, indicating no restriction-driven suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate a collapse in commuting-linked trip chains; when both series drop together, the loss of incidental retail stops embedded in commutes compounds to depress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict, over a 4-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -10.1 to -22.4 and TRANSIT fell from -31.4 to -44.6 over the same t-3w to t-1w window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers in line with either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone recovering, showing no compounded interaction effect beyond single-series explanatory power.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation of RESIDENTIAL mobility above +5 points signals an active stay-at-home regime driven by policy or advisory measures, which structurally caps RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks until RESIDENTIAL mobility normalizes.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 4.9, 5.1, 8.9, 6.4 across the four weeks, staying elevated throughout
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 points, contradicting the capping mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound from -43.7 to -28.0 suggests households are substituting outdoor park visits for indoor retail and recreation trips, which will continue to divert footfall away from RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -43.7 at t-1w to -28.0 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC only partially recovered
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with PARKS over the next week, indicating the two series are complements rather than substitutes.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized weekly dip-and-recovery pattern across PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC at t-1w resembles a recurring weekly or short-term seasonal event (e.g., a public holiday or long weekend) whose effect dissipates within one week, allowing RETAIL_REC to return to its pre-dip baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all dipped simultaneously at t-1w and partially recovered at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to return toward its t-2w level within one week and instead remains depressed or declines further.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained close to baseline (within +/-2 points) across all four weeks, indicating essential-trip demand is stable and not substituting for discretionary retail; this stability implies RETAIL_REC's future direction is driven by discretionary-sector dynamics rather than essential-good constraints, supporting continued gradual decline consistent with the broader downward drift seen at t-1w.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within -1.1 to 2.1 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, indicating discretionary retail is decoupled from the essential-trip baseline as hypothesized.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises at the same time WORKPLACES mobility falls, the combination signals a shift to home-centered routines (remote work plus reduced outside obligations) that jointly depresses RETAIL_REC more than either trend alone, over a two-week window.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week while WORKPLACES falls week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.1 to 8.9 while WORKPLACES fell from -12.6 to -22.4 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further over the next 2 weeks even when RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls concurrently, undermining the joint home-centered routine mechanism.
